body.br:
1. A shaped aircraft fuel cell comprising a through-void defined through the shaped fuel cell, or an edge cavity defined along an edge of the shaped fuel cell, the through-void or the edge cavity corresponding to an aircraft structure that translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into a fuel cell area of the aircraft.
2. The shaped fuel cell of claim 1, wherein the shaped fuel cell comprises:
one or more through-voids, each through-void corresponding to a respective aircraft structure that translates, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft; and/or
one or more edge cavities, each edge cavity corresponding to a respective aircraft structure that translates, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft.
3. The shaped fuel cell of claim 1, wherein the aircraft structure translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft is pushed into the fuel cell area of the aircraft by impact of the aircraft with a surface.
4. The shaped fuel cell of claim 1, wherein the aircraft structure that translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft is pushed upward into the fuel cell area of the aircraft by impact of the aircraft with the surface.
5. The shaped fuel cell of claim 1, wherein the aircraft structure that translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft is pushed downward, by inertia, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft by impact of the aircraft with the surface.
6. The shaped fuel cell of claim 1, wherein the drop impact of the aircraft is a crash.
7. The shaped fuel cell of claim 1, wherein the drop impact of the aircraft is a drop test.
8. An aircraft comprising:
an area designated to house a fuel cell;
an aircraft structure that translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into the area designated to house the fuel cell;
a shaped fuel cell comprising a through-void defined through the shaped fuel cell, and/or
an edge cavity defined along an edge of the shaped fuel cell, the through-void and/or the edge cavity corresponding to the aircraft structure that translates, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the area of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cell.
9. The aircraft of claim 8, wherein the aircraft comprises a plurality of areas designated to house fuel cells and a plurality of aircraft structures that translate, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into one or more the areas designated to house the fuel cells, and the aircraft further comprise a plurality of shaped fuel cells, each respective shaped fuel cell comprising one or more through-voids defined through the respective shaped fuel cell, and/or one or more edge cavities defined along one or more edges of each respective shaped fuel cell, the one or more through- voids and/or one or more edge cavities, each corresponding to a respective one of the aircraft structures that translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into a respective one of the areas of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cells.
10. The aircraft of claim 8, wherein the aircraft is a rotorcraft.
11. The aircraft of claim 8, , wherein the drop impact of the aircraft is a crash.
12. The aircraft of claim 8, wherein the drop impact of the aircraft is a drop test.
13. The aircraft of claim 8, wherein the aircraft structure that translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into the area of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cell is pushed into the area of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cell as a result of impact of the aircraft with a surface.
14. The aircraft of claim 8, wherein the aircraft structure that translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into the area of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cell is pushed upward into the area of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cell by impact of the aircraft with a surface.
15. The aircraft of claim 8, wherein the aircraft structure that translates, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into the area of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cell is pushed downward, by inertia, into the area of the aircraft designated to house the fuel cell by impact of the aircraft with a surface.
16. A method for preventing rupture of fuel cells in an aircraft during a drop impact of the aircraft comprising:
reviewing layout of an aircraft and determining aircraft structures that will translate, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into a fuel cell area of the aircraft;
providing a shaped fuel cell comprising:
defining one or more through-voids in the shaped fuel cell, each through-void corresponding to an aircraft structure determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft; and/or
defining one or more edge cavities in the shaped fuel cell, each edge cavity corresponding to an aircraft structure determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft; and
installing the shaped fuel cell in the fuel cell area of the aircraft with the one or more through voids and/or the one or more edge cavities corresponding to the aircraft structure determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft.
17. The method of claim 16, further comprising receiving and accommodating, by each of the one or more through-voids and/or the one or more edge cavities, a respective aircraft structure that was determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the fuel cell area of the aircraft, pushed into the fuel cell area of the aircraft by impact of the aircraft with a surface, preventing rupture of the shaped fuel cell by the respective aircraft structure.
18. The method of claim 16, wherein the drop impact of the aircraft is a drop test.
19. The method of claim 16, wherein the aircraft comprises a plurality of fuel cell areas and a plurality of shaped fuel cells and the method further comprises:
reviewing layout of the aircraft and determining aircraft structures that will translate, during a drop impact of the aircraft, into each fuel cell area of the aircraft;
providing the shaped fuel cells comprising:
defining one or more through-voids in each respective shaped fuel cell, each through-void corresponding to a respective aircraft structure determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into a respective fuel cell area of the aircraft;
and/or defining one or more edge cavities in each respective shaped fuel cell, each edge cavity corresponding to a respective aircraft structure determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the respective fuel cell area of the aircraft; and
installing the respective shaped fuel cells in the respective fuel cell areas of the aircraft, with each of the one or more through voids and/or each of the one or more edge cavities corresponding to the respective aircraft structure determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into the respective fuel cell areas of the aircraft.
20. The method of claim 19, further comprising receiving and accommodating, by each of the one or more through-voids and/or the one or more edge cavities, the respective aircraft structure that was determined to translate, during the drop impact of the aircraft, into a respective fuel cell area of the aircraft, pushed into the respective fuel cell area of the aircraft by impact of the aircraft with a surface, preventing rupture of the shaped fuel cells by the aircraft structures, during the drop impact of the aircraft. -18- -19- -20- -21- -22- -23-
